sections.question: How many thousand barrels per day higher were Chevron's U.S. refinery crude unit inputs in the second quarter of 2026 than in the quarter when Chevron acquired its majority stake in ACES Delta?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Doc 4: capex in the third quarter of 2024 was down "largely due to the absence of the third quarter 2023 acquisition of a majority stake in ACES Delta, LLC", so the acquisition quarter is the third quarter of 2023.

Step 2. Doc 4: its U.S. downstream table (columns 3Q 2024, 2Q 2024, 3Q 2023, then year-to-date) gives refinery crude unit inputs, which include crude oil and other inputs, of 980 thousand barrels per day for the third quarter of 2023.

Step 3. Doc 12: U.S. refinery crude unit inputs were 1,070 thousand barrels per day in the second quarter of 2026.

Step 4. Doc 4 and Doc 12: difference = 1,070 - 980 = 90 (thousand barrels per day).

Decoy check. Doc 1 and Doc 12: Doc 1 prints "Refinery Crude Oil Inputs" of 961 for the third quarter of 2023, a narrower crude-oil-only measure, which would give 1,070 - 961 = 109.

Decoy check. Doc 4 and Doc 12: Doc 4's year-to-date 2023 column (965) would give 1,070 - 965 = 105.
